subject: GPU pool sizing validation and commercial ask
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jill Park <jill.park@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU pool sizing validation and commercial ask

Hi Jill —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I sketched a conservative starting point for a Dedicated commit and what we’d include in an acceptance test. Attaching a brief sketch (initial-sizing-sketch.pdf). High level:

- Nimbus target: sustained user-facing throughput for inference pipelines, roughly 6k tokens/sec across peak window, with p95 latency target <200ms for 512-token requests.
- Typical request shape: 300–700 tokens, mix of short completions + one-shot summarization.
- Security: private VPC; SOC2 evidence under separate thread.

Questions for you (quick):
1) Do you want guarantees expressed in tokens/sec or reqs/sec (or both)?
2) Are you expecting steady-state >=6k tokens/sec or brief spikes to 12k tokens/sec?
3) Acceptance window preference: 30-minute sustained run vs 1-hour run?

We can size an H100-equivalent GPU pool and propose commit bands. Karthik cc’d here will propose the measurement methodology we’d use to verify tokens/sec and latency.

If those answers are good, I’ll put together a formal offer (commit + discounts + SLA credits + acceptance plan).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Jill Park <jill.park@nimbushealth.com>

Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU pool sizing validation and commercial ask

Vanessa, thanks — this is helpful. Quick answers below: 

- We prefer guarantees in both tokens/sec and requests/sec. Our analytics team reports in rps, but cost modeling is tokens-based. For our initial procurement ask: baseline guarantee of 6,000 tokens/sec sustained, and the ability to absorb 12,000 tokens/sec bursts for up to 10 minutes.
- Request mix: median request ~420 tokens; p95 ~1,100 tokens. So the rps target for 6k tokens/sec is roughly 14–16 rps sustained (depending on avg tokens). We’ll want you to show both numbers in the acceptance test.
- Latency SLO: p95 <200ms, p99 <450ms for our interactive pipelines (512 token cap). Batch-only jobs can have higher latency.
- Acceptance window: prefer a 30-minute sustained run for baseline, plus 3 spot 10-minute spike runs to validate burst handling. Measurement should exclude cold-start variance and note warm-cache conditions.

We’ll also need:
- A proposed commit length and discount tiers (12 vs 24 month).
- Clarity on how quantization/precision affects guarantees (do you guarantee at FP16/Half, or will quantized 4-bit models be treated as different SKUs?).
- A simple failure credits table (if tokens/sec falls below band during acceptance).

I’ll loop in procurement if we get to commercial terms.

Thanks,
Jill Park
VP Engineering, Nimbus Health
jill.park@nimbushealth.com

Subject: Re: GPU pool sizing validation and commercial ask (measurement methodology draft)

Folks — drafting the measurement methodology we should propose to Nimbus. High-level notes and open decisions below; I’ll attach a polished PDF (throughput-measurement-protocol.pdf) for the offer.

1) Measurement targets to report (both):
   - Sustained tokens/sec (30-minute sliding window), measured at the service ingress point.
   - Req/s measured at the same ingress, with tokens-per-request histogram.
   - Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) for the matched request class (<=512 tokens).

2) Warm vs cold cache:
   - Acceptance runs must be performed following a 15-minute warm-up window to populate prefix/KV caches; the 30-minute acceptance window starts after warm-up.

3) Spike validation:
   - Three 10-minute spike runs at 2x baseline (approx 12k tokens/sec) with identical request mix. If a spike run fails, engineerable fallback & mitigation must be documented; failing 2/3 spike attempts triggers credit remediation.

4) Hardware and model configuration baseline:
   - Reference hardware: H100-equivalent instances with 80GB GPU memory (or agreed equivalent).
   - Baseline model config: FP16 execution path, kv-prefix caching enabled, batching set to keep p95 below 200ms for 512-token requests. Quantized models (4-bit) will be treated as a different performance SKU and not included in the FP16 guarantee unless explicitly tested.

5) Sample correctness and tolerances:
   - Metrics collected from the serving proxy (token-stream counters + request ids). Tolerances: +/-3% on sustained tokens/sec over the 30-minute window.

6) Acceptance test harness and tooling:
   - We’ll provide runbench.py (based on our internal continuous-batching harness) and a k6/Locust load profile reproducer. The harness will record request/response traces and attach a run artifact. 

7) Credits and remediation:
   - If sustained tokens/sec falls below 90% of committed band during the acceptance window, customer may elect remediation run or apply a credit equal to X% of the monthly committed fee (table in attached doc).

Open questions we should confirm with Sales: discount request range, whether Nimbus wants SLA in tokens/sec or optional latency-bound SLA, and commit length sensitivity.

I’ll finalize the PDF and the commit-size table (nimbus-commit-matrix.xlsx) for Vanessa to include in the commercial email.

—Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: throughput-measurement-protocol.pdf

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU pool sizing validation and commercial ask — proposed commit and acceptance plan

Hi Jill (and procurement),

Appreciate the specificity — based on Karthik’s measurement methodology and your inputs we propose the following commercial package for a 12-month reserved commit: 

Offer summary (12-month)
- Commit: 8 H100-equivalent GPUs reserved (dedicated pool).
- Baseline guarantee: 6,000 tokens/sec sustained (measured as 30-minute sliding window post warm-up).
- Burst envelope: validated ability to reach 12,000 tokens/sec for three 10-minute spike runs during acceptance.
- Latency SLO: p95 <200ms, p99 <450ms for the <=512-token request class (measured same window).
- Discount: 20% off list for 12-month commit; 28% for 24-month commit (see attached matrix).
- Credits: If baseline sustained throughput <90% of band during acceptance, either one remediation run or a credit equal to 10% of that month’s committed fee. Failure to meet latency SLOs during acceptance triggers partial credit (table attached).
- Acceptance test: 15-minute warm-up, 30-minute sustained baseline run, three 10-minute spike runs. We’ll run the test jointly (Redwood runbench.py + Nimbus verification).
- Model config: FP16 path used for guarantees; quantized (4-bit) variants are optional and must be separately validated if Nimbus wants to use them for cost savings without losing guarantee coverage.

Next steps:
1) If procurement is comfortable, we’ll share a formal term sheet + DocuSign link and schedule an acceptance-run kickoff (you pick a 2-hour window next week).
2) We’ll push the throughput-measurement-protocol.pdf and the nimbus-commit-matrix.xlsx to the HubSpot deal and share Drive link.

I’ve attached the formal plan and the sizing matrix for reference. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through the acceptance steps.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198
